newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: A total 37,500 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 43.069 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Out of this, traders in France received 31,500 tonnes and in Denmark 6,000 tonnes, it added.

This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 2.033 million tonnes. This compares with the 54,250 tonnes awarded on May 22, 1996, when the cumulative tonnage totalled 2.158 million tonnes.
Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to end-September to be 43.069 Ecus per 100 kilos, the exact amount awarded.
Traders had also forecast the total authorised sugar tonnage export awards to be between 40,000 and 45,000 tonnes versus 70,100 last week when the restitution was 43.042 Ecus.
